The Bengal Renaissance was a burst of social reform, writing and new thought in Bengal under British rule, centred on Calcutta, from the late 1700s to the early 1900s.

A new Bengali middle class, schooled in both English and Indian learning, asked what in their society should change:

  • Ram Mohan Roy, often called its father, fought sati and founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828.
  • Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar won the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856.
  • Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's Anandamath gave India the song "Vande Mataram".
  • Swami Vivekananda carried a reformed Hinduism abroad.

It is often said to end with Rabindranath Tagore, Nobel laureate in 1913, who died in 1941. It was mostly a movement of upper-caste Hindu men, but its ideas fed Indian nationalism.
sum: The Bengal Renaissance was a burst of social reform, writing and new thought in Bengal under British rule, centred on Calcutta, from the late 1700s to the early 1900s.
